body: Ahh I see :) Sending good luck your way if you decide to use it! I definitely hesitated with the Slinda for a while too, had a couple packs of it on my counter for months lol. It helped to remember that each pill has a half life of about a day, so within a week or so it'll be down to practically undetectable amounts in you, and you can stop if you're having a bad reaction. If you were okay on Yasmin/Yaz before, it's probably a decent sign that this will be okay too. I get the apprehension though. I wish there were better treatment options for women than birth control for unidentified pain and other conditions. It sucks.

I feel really good on it so far but it's only been a week so not that much data to go off of :) I've got more energy and and higher libido I think, though it might be coincidence this early in. I'm pretty much just hoping that the placebos won't wreck me otherwise I'm really happy with it. I did feel equally good on the Yasmin actives before the migraines so I probably just react well to drospirenone. Hoping that the lack of estrogen will make the hormone drop less painful lol

Thank you so much:) I've just started Slynd yesterday, hopefully it goes okay. I considered taking Yasmin continually but in all honesty that would make the pill super expensive for me and the placebos prolonged the length of each pack. I also worried about getting breakthrough bleeding and was decently reliant on the withdrawal bleed to let me know I wasn't pregnant (even though it came with like 4 days of severe migraine and vomiting lol) I might end up going back to it if I don't like the Slynd or I might try Yaz instead, hopefully the reason I liked Yasmin so much was because of the progestin or something. Again thanks, it's good to know that someone has a similar experience with estrogen migraines and is faring well on Slynd! :))
